description:
Lists checklist rules as records, filtered by component, ID, scope, layer, level or check. Each rule has a stable ID to cite in reviews and commits, its level (must or should), its scope, its requirement, how to check it (like a unit test, a review or axe's button-name rule) and a link to it.

WHEN TO USE: to review code rule by rule, to get only the rules that apply to a task, to look rules up by ID, or to find the ones a tool can check. Pass scope ["component", "both"] to build or review a component, and ["usage", "both"] to review a screen that uses it.
WHEN NOT TO USE: for a component's API, DOM contract and tokens, use get-contract, which has every rule too.

It returns up to 50 rules at a time, and total counts every rule that matches. When there are more, pass nextOffset as offset, with the same filters, to get the next page.

A component meets the standard when it meets every must rule. Each should rule is expected unless there's a good reason not to follow it.

automated.description: true for the rules tools check all of (unit tests, axe, a type check, a linter or a visual regression test), false for the ones a person checks, at least in part.

component.description: The component or foundation, like button or design-tokens.

ids.description: The IDs of the rules to look up, like ["button/keep-focus"].

layer.description: ui (how it looks), ux (user experience), dx (developer experience) or ax (agentic experience).

limit.description: How many rules to return, at most.

offset.description: Where the page starts: 0, or the nextOffset of the page before.

scope.description: Who meets the rule: component (the component itself), usage (the code that uses it) or both. Rules without a scope, like the Design Tokens', match any scope.

name: list-rules

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page, when there is one.

automated.description: Whether tools check all of it.

axe.description: The axe rules that check it.

total.description: How many rules match, on every page.

unknown.description: The IDs asked for that no rule has, with the ones that might have been meant.

title: List Rules
